skill.name: x402socks
skill.description: Inspect x402socks plans and manage access to TLS proxy egress for authorized jobs. Purchases use USDC on Base and require a configured signer and explicit approval.
skill.summary: Review proxy quotes and manage short-lived access for authorized network jobs.
skill.author: x402socks

security_audit.summary: Most scanner matches are Markdown formatting, ordinary credential handling, or documented network calls. The review found gaps in destination controls, one-time payment approval, and credential handling. No evidence of embedded malware, deliberate credential harvesting, or reviewer-targeted prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Destination checks cover only the first URL in some clients.
remediation.suggestion: Reject redirects by default. Enforce the authorized HTTPS host list on every browser request, including subresources, or omit browser examples that cannot enforce it.

remediation.issue: The signing client trusts a reusable approval record and does not pin the purchase origin.
remediation.suggestion: Issue authenticated approvals through the operator interface and atomically reserve each approval before signing. Pin the provider HTTPS origin, reject redirects, and reconcile settlement before any retry.

remediation.issue: Legacy browser guidance and a shipped test override permit unsafe credential transports.
remediation.suggestion: Remove legacy credential use instructions. Move alternate endpoint testing into a separate harness that accepts only disposable fixtures and cannot read live credentials.

remediation.issue: Standalone recipes bypass credential file checks and safe configuration serialization.
remediation.suggestion: Reuse the checked token reader and configuration serializer. Require owner-only regular credential files and verify recovery proof files before reading them.

remediation.issue: The quote succeeds without a cap, and provider text reaches the approval workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Require a finite cap for a successful guarded quote. Validate response field types and lengths, and render remote descriptions as untrusted data.

remediation.issue: The egress test discloses the original IP address to a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the direct check before running it and require explicit opt-in. Let the operator use an approved IP check service.

content.user_title: Review Quotes for Authorized Proxy Access
content.value_statement: Authorized network checks may need a temporary egress location with a clear cost. This skill shows live proxy terms and documents an approval step before payment.
actual_capabilities: Check provider health and list exits marked healthy and enabled.
Read catalog prices and decode live HTTP 402 terms without signing a payment.
Document an approval workflow for purchases using USDC on Base and a separately configured signer.
Store tokens privately and request token status, validation, rotation, or recovery.
Compare direct and proxied egress addresses using an external IP check service.
limitations: A purchase requires a funded Base wallet and a signer supplied by the operator.
The helper checks a quote against a spending cap only when a cap is provided.
Browser examples do not enforce the authorized host list for all requests.
The egress test sends the original egress address to an external IP check service.

use_cases.title: Compare options before approving spend
use_cases.description: Review live prices and included limits without using a wallet or creating a payment.

use_cases.title: Plan a regional service check
use_cases.description: Review available exit regions for an owned service and record which destinations are authorized.

use_cases.title: Triage lost proxy access
use_cases.description: Use redacted status and settlement information to decide whether recovery is appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Check service readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize provider health and the healthy exit regions. Do not test a target or use a token.

prompt_templates.title: Review a capped quote
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the live quote for [package] with a maximum of [amount] USDC. Report the price, limits, and recipient without signing or paying.

prompt_templates.title: Review an approved job
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [approved terms] with [redacted quote] and flag every mismatch. Check the approved host list separately and stop without making requests.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile a provisioning failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [redacted error] and [settlement status]. Explain whether recovery is appropriate and what approval is missing, without signing, rotating, or purchasing.

output_examples.input: Review a quote for a six-hour package with a 1.00 USDC cap.
output_examples.output: Illustrative result: The quote requests 1.00 USDC on Base for six hours and up to 1 GB. No payment was signed.

output_examples.input: Review a failed provisioning report after a confirmed settlement.
output_examples.output: Settlement is recorded, but provisioning failed. Request approval for token recovery instead of paying again.

output_examples.input: Review an authorized destination list for an owned service.
output_examples.output: The starting hostname matches the list. Redirects and embedded requests still need enforcement before browser testing.

best_practices: Set an explicit cap and verify current terms, the provider origin, and the signer before recording one-time approval.
Keep tokens in private files and use TLS with certificate verification for all credential transfers.
Enforce the approved destination list on every request and disclose any direct IP check before running it.
anti_patterns: Treating a successful quote or an earlier approval as permission to sign again.
Printing reusable credentials, recovery proofs, or raw payment responses in logs or chat.
Using alternate egress to bypass a block, rate limit, or access decision.

faq.question: Does checking a quote spend USDC?
faq.answer: No. A quote reads the payment challenge without signing. Set a cap if the quote must enforce a budget.

faq.question: What wallet does a purchase require?
faq.answer: A purchase requires an EVM-compatible wallet funded with USDC on Base and a signer configured by the operator.

faq.question: Does the Bash helper sign purchases?
faq.answer: No. It quotes terms and manages tokens. Payment signing requires a separate client or signer workflow.

faq.question: What transport does the helper use?
faq.answer: It uses TLS HTTP CONNECT for proxy traffic. Legacy SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT do not protect the reusable token on the proxy hop.

faq.question: Does the proxy grant permission to reach a target?
faq.answer: No. Follow the target rules and enforce an explicit list of authorized hosts throughout the job.

faq.question: What happens if payment settles but access is not provisioned?
faq.answer: Reconcile the payment first. The documented recovery process uses the settlement transaction hash and a fresh proof from the paying wallet.
